findings.reason: The protected Python solution implements Node and TreeBuilder classes to construct and evaluate binary expression trees from postfix token arrays. It uses an explicit stack during postfix parsing to build ExpressionNode subtrees, then computes expression values via recursive evaluate() calls. The solution runs in O(t) time and O(t) space; no candidate is required.
Postfix stack invariant ensures operators pop right then left subtrees in correct evaluation order. Recursive tree evaluate() applies +, -, *, / with truncating integer division.

Building tree from t tokens takes O(t) stack pushes/pops. Evaluating tree takes O(t) structural recursion calls. Auxiliary space is O(t) for tree nodes and evaluation call stack. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts postfix array, with TreeBuilder returning root Node whose evaluate() method returns the integer result.

The approach accurately details postfix stack invariant construction, separate ExpressionNode evaluation logic, truncating division handling, and O(t) time / O(t) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover tree-less integer stack calculation, recursive right-to-left parsing complexity, front-based list shift quadratic costs, single operand leaf nodes, operator right-before-left operand ordering rules, negative intermediate values, and zero-truncation vs floor division.
